newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mark down vs dollar, yen in Tokyo on French vote.
newsitem.headline: Mark down vs dollar, yen in Tokyo on French vote.

text.p: *Mark fell against dollar and yen in early Tokyo as traders began selling marks in reaction to triumph by France's Socialist-led opposition in Sunday's decisive second-round runoff.
*Although victory by left-wing parties mostly anticipated, image of weak euro caused wave of mark sales, dealers said.
*Dollar/yen stuck near 116 yen, top-heavy above 116.50 yen with steady exporter offers. So far, no substantial bids detected in dollar/yen trade.
*A trust bank dealer said mark/yen could be technically supported near 67.75 yen, but dip towards 67.50 yen possible if it clearly breaks through that point.
*Dollar could eventually aim for 1.72 mark level, dealers said. But a city bank dealer said possible buying back of marks would halt its rise if mark jumps against French franc later in day.
*Franc had lost ground through Sunday evening after voting ended at 1800 GMT and projections showed a left-wing win, dipping to 3.3840/45 per mark at 2305 GMT from 3.3816 late on Friday.

*"Now the effectiveness of European economic and monetary union (EMU) is in question," another trust bank dealer said. He added that image of weak euro and open conflict between German government and Bundesbank over possible revaluation of its gold reserves have been causing mark sales.

*Combined left won an absolute majority of at least 289 seats in France's parliamentary election on Sunday. Socialist Party is committed to launching single currency, but is demanding flexible interpretation of Maastricht Treaty, European "economic government", and early membership for Italy, Spain and Portugal in EMU.

*Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, who will be asked to form a government on Monday, said people had voted for a change of direction in European policy, but he did not call into question planned single European currency.
*In Germany, ruling coalition said on Monday it still wants to revalue Bundesbank's gold and currency reserves this year.
*"I think there won't be so many traders who want to buy marks aggressively," said the first trust bank dealer.
*Mark/yen stood near 67.76/79 yen at 0049 GMT, while dollar/mark was at 1.7155/60 marks.
